sections.title: Mission & Identity
data: JBSA-Fort Sam Houston is a center of U.S. military medicine. Its signature tenant is Brooke Army Medical Center (BAMC), the largest military healthcare organization in the Department of Defense and the sole Level I Trauma Center within the Military Health System.

The post also hosts the Medical Education & Training Campus (METC), which trains Army, Navy and Air Force enlisted medical personnel in 49 courses (more than 16,500 graduates a year projected at peak capacity), plus the U.S. Army Medical Center of Excellence (MEDCoE). Installation support is provided by the Air Force's 502d Air Base Wing.

data.subtitle: Fort Sam Houston is home to Brooke Army Medical Center, the primary military emergency department in San Antonio, and to the military's enlisted medical training campus.
intro: Brooke Army Medical Center serves more than 240,000 military beneficiaries across the San Antonio area. It is the sole Level I Trauma Center within the Military Health System and the primary emergency department for the San Antonio military health system, a role that grew when Wilford Hall's emergency department on Lackland became an urgent care center on April 4, 2026.

For many service members, an assignment here is tied to medical training or care, given METC and MEDCoE. It has a different feel from an operational post, more campus and care than flight line or motor pool.

recommendations.advice: BAMC serves the whole San Antonio military community; confirm enrollment and referrals through TRICARE West.

Alamo Heights and Terrell Hills are about 16 to 18 minutes from BAMC with no traffic. Alamo Heights ISD takes no transfer students, and Terrell Hills lists both Alamo Heights ISD and North East ISD, so confirm the district for any address.
You're minutes from downtown: the River Walk, the Pearl, and the rest of San Antonio.

sections.title: Gates & Access
data: Open 24 hours: Walters Gate, the BAMC/I-35 gate and Harry Wurzbach East, plus the Camp Bullis gate. New Braunfels, BAMC Beach and Winans open only at weekday rush hours (afternoons are outbound only at New Braunfels and BAMC Beach), Schofield is open weekdays 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., and Harry Wurzbach West and Wilson are closed.

Visitors without a DoD ID need a visitor pass and, since May 7, 2025, a REAL ID. The BAMC/I-35 Visitor Center (Bldg. 4299, George Beach Ave, 210-539-9826) is open 24 hours; the Walters Visitor Center (Bldg. 892, Hood St, 210-221-2650) is open weekdays 7:30 a.m. to 3 p.m. Hours change, so confirm on the official gate page before you go.

sections.title: On-Base Housing
data: On-post family housing is Fort Sam Houston Family Housing, managed by Hunt Military Communities since June 2021: 925 homes in eight neighborhoods, five of them wholly or partly historic, from 2-bedroom homes at Patch Chaffee to 5-bedroom homes at Gorgas Circle.
No wait list is posted, and Hunt advertised immediate availability for active-duty members in November 2026. Military Housing Office: 3171 Zinn Road, Bldg. 1161, (210) 221-0881.

sections.title: Schools
data: On post, schooling is the Fort Sam Houston Independent School District (FSHISD), a Texas public district physically on the installation (Fort Sam Houston Elementary; Robert G. Cole Middle/High). It earned an A (95) in Texas's 2026 ratings, with a 98.3% graduation rate for the class of 2025. It is not a DoDEA district.

Children living on post attend automatically and come first. Children living off post need a Non-Resident Transfer, approved one year at a time and limited by space, and the district says it can't accept off-post elementary students who need resource-classroom instruction or speech therapy. District office: 210-368-8707.

Off post, school assignment depends on your address. Alamo Heights ISD (B, 88 in 2026) takes no transfer students, North East ISD earned a B (81), San Antonio ISD a C (75) and Judson ISD a C (71), so confirm the specific district and campus for any address.

intro: Whether to rent or buy is the biggest money decision of most PCS moves, and the answer is mostly about how long you'll be here and how steady the local market is.
rent: Your tour is short (about two years or less) or your orders feel uncertain.
You want time to learn the area before committing to a neighborhood.
You'd rather not gamble on resale timing when you PCS out.
Your BAH comfortably covers rent in the areas you'd consider.
buy: You expect to be here three or more years.
You want to use your VA loan and build equity instead of paying rent.
The market is steady and you could rent the home out later if needed.
You've found a neighborhood and commute you're confident about.
data.bottom_line: There is no universal right answer. Run your BAH against the rent and home prices above, weigh your tour length and the local market, and talk to a lender and an agent who work with military families before you commit.

intro: The first month at a new duty station is mostly logistics. Knocking these out early makes everything else easier.

steps.title: Line up temporary lodging
steps.text: Book on-base lodging or a short-term rental before you arrive. You can claim Temporary Lodging Expense (TLE) for a limited number of days while you house-hunt.

steps.title: In-process and update DEERS
steps.text: Report to your unit and finance, and make sure DEERS and ID cards are current for every family member so TRICARE and base access work.

steps.title: Start with the Housing Office
steps.text: Check on-base availability and get the housing office's read on off-base neighborhoods before you sign anything.

steps.title: Register your vehicle and sort access
steps.text: Handle base access and vehicle registration, and learn the visitor-pass process for guests. Bring your registration and insurance.

steps.title: Enroll the kids in school
steps.text: Contact the gaining school district or DoDEA early and bring records and immunizations. The School Liaison Office can help with the transfer.

steps.title: Set up healthcare
steps.text: Update your TRICARE region and enrollment so you can be seen at the local military treatment facility or network providers.

data.q: What makes Fort Sam Houston unique?
data.a: It is a center of military medicine, home to Brooke Army Medical Center (the sole Level I Trauma Center within the Military Health System) and the medical training campuses, METC and MEDCoE.

Close-in choices include Alamo Heights and Terrell Hills (about 16 to 18 minutes to BAMC with no traffic), Windcrest and the northeast side (about 14 to 20 minutes) and Stone Oak on the north side (about 32 minutes). On-post housing is run by Hunt Military Communities: 925 homes in eight neighborhoods.
BAMC is the sole Level I Trauma Center within the Military Health System and serves more than 240,000 beneficiaries in the San Antonio area. Confirm enrollment through TRICARE West.
MHA TX285 (San Antonio), shared with the other JBSA bases. Use the calculator above.

picks.name: San Antonio River Walk
picks.blurb: The city's signature network of riverside walkways, restaurants, and boat tours, just below street level downtown.

picks.name: The Pearl
picks.blurb: A former brewery turned dining and shopping district north of downtown, with a popular weekend farmers market.

picks.name: San Antonio Missions National Historical Park
